definitionEn: an occasion when a group of people come together for a shared purpose
situation: A number of people meet together in one place, often socially or to mark a special occasion.

examples.text: The wedding ended with a small family [[gathering]] at her parents' house.
Police were called to break up an unauthorised political [[gathering]] in the city square.
Every Friday evening, the book club holds a small [[gathering]] at the local café.

texts: Neighbours organised a small [[gathering]] to welcome the new family on the street.
The annual sales [[gathering]] brings staff from every branch together.
A storm forced them to cancel the outdoor [[gathering]].

badCollocation.text: make a [[gathering]] for the whole team
badCollocation.noteRu: Собрание, встречу обычно organise или hold, а не make: hold a gathering, organise a gathering.

collocationTask.prompt: Every August the whole family holds a big ___ at the lake house.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Собрание, встреча людей — a gathering. Audition — прослушивание, inspection — проверка, invoice — счёт; ни одно не про встречу семьи.

nuance.text: After the funeral, family and friends went back to the house for a quiet [[gathering]].
nuance.explanationRu: Gathering — неформальная встреча людей по случаю (праздник, поминки, приезд гостей). Meeting — рабочая встреча с конкретной повесткой; после похорон meeting прозвучит слишком по-деловому.

reverse.text: The whole team has a [[meeting]] every Monday morning to plan the week.
reverse.explanationRu: Рабочая встреча с чёткой повесткой — meeting. Gathering подойдёт для неформального сбора, а не для планового рабочего совещания.

fixIt.text: After the funeral, the whole family held a small [[meeting]] just to sit together quietly and share memories over tea.
fixIt.explanationRu: Meeting подразумевает деловую повестку, а тут «просто посидеть вместе и повспоминать за чаем» — явное противоречие. Неформальная встреча — gathering.

wordFormation.text: Friends and neighbours held a small [[gathering]] to celebrate her retirement.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Are you doing anything for your birthday this year?"
options: Just a small gathering at my flat, nothing fancy.
Just a small gathering at my flat, we're voting on the new budget.
A modest convocation of associates shall be assembled at my residence.
reply.explanationRu: Gathering — неформальная встреча по случаю праздника. Голосование по бюджету (второй вариант) больше подходит для meeting, а не для дружеского gathering. Третий звучит как официальное объявление, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: About twenty relatives met at their grandmother's house for Sunday lunch.
rewrite.frame: About twenty relatives came to a family ____ at their grandmother's house for Sunday lunch.

definitionEn: to look steadily at someone or something for a long time, often in admiration or deep thought
situation: Someone looks at a person, view or object for a long time without moving their eyes away, often with strong feeling.

examples.text: He [[gazed]] at her across the crowded room, unable to look away.
Tourists stood at the viewpoint, [[gazing]] out over the misty valley below.
She likes to [[gaze]] out of the office window whenever she needs to think.

texts: She likes to [[gaze]] at the stars from her balcony.
Try not to [[gaze]] at your phone during the interview.
He would often [[gaze]] into the fire, lost in thought.

badCollocation.noteRu: Gaze — долгий, пристальный взгляд, несовместим с quickly. Быстро взглянуть — glance at your watch.

collocationTask.prompt: From the top of the hill, they ___ out over the entire valley in silence.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Долгий взгляд на пейзаж — gazed. Blinked — «моргнули», waved — «помахали», coughed — «кашлянули»; ни одно не про взгляд вдаль.

nuance.text: The little boy [[gazed]] at the birthday cake in complete wonder.
nuance.explanationRu: Gaze — смотреть долго, с восхищением, нежностью или задумчивостью. Stare — тоже долгий взгляд, но часто невежливый или недоумевающий; для восхищения ребёнка точнее gaze.

reverse.text: It's rude to [[stare]] at people just because they look different.
reverse.explanationRu: Невежливый, пристальный взгляд, часто с недоумением, — stare. Gaze обычно не звучит грубо, поэтому в предупреждениях о невежливости используют stare.

fixIt.text: He [[glanced]] at the sunset for almost ten minutes, completely mesmerised by the colours.
fixIt.explanationRu: Glance — короткий, быстрый взгляд, а тут «почти десять минут, заворожённо» — явное противоречие. Долгий взгляд — gazed.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What were you doing just standing by the window for so long?"
options: Sorry, I was just gazing out at the sunset, lost in thought.
Sorry, I was just gazing for two seconds, then I left.
I was merely engaging in prolonged ocular fixation upon the horizon.
reply.explanationRu: Gaze — долгий взгляд, поэтому for two seconds во втором варианте противоречит смыслу слова. Третий звучит как медицинский отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: For a long moment, she just looked at the ring without saying a word.
rewrite.frame: For a long moment, she just ____ at the ring without saying a word.

definitionEn: a particular level of effort, speed or intensity, especially one that can be increased
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «прибавить обороты, выйти на новый уровень усилий» (move up a gear, shift into a higher gear); бытовые значения «снаряжение» (camping gear) или «передача в машине» (first gear) проще и не тренируются напрямую.
situation: A person, team or campaign increases its pace, effort or intensity, especially after a slow start.

examples.text: United need to move up a [[gear]] if they want to win the title this season.
After a slow start, the fundraising campaign finally shifted into a higher [[gear]] in its final week.
With exams only two weeks away, it's time to move up a [[gear]] and start revising properly.

texts: By half-time, the team had moved up a [[gear]] and dominated the match.
The campaign really shifted into top [[gear]] during the final month.
It's time for this project to move into a higher [[gear]].

badCollocation.noteRu: С gear в этом значении не говорят increase: move up a gear, shift into a higher gear, step up a gear — но не increase a gear.

collocationTask.prompt: The negotiations need to move up a ___ if they're going to meet Friday's deadline.
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Прибавить обороты, ускориться» — move up a gear. Size, grade и decade по смыслу сюда не подходят вовсе.

nuance.text: The team needs to move up a [[gear]] in the second half if they want to catch up.
nuance.explanationRu: Gear — конкретный, ощутимый скачок на новый уровень усилий (move up a gear). Pace — сама скорость, без идеи резкого переключения: increase the pace, а не increase the gear.

reverse.text: Marathon runners must learn to keep a steady [[pace]] rather than sprinting early on.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о ровной, постоянной скорости — pace. Gear предполагает переключение на новый уровень, а не поддержание одного и того же темпа.

fixIt.text: With the deadline just days away, the whole team needs to move into a higher [[stage]] and finish the report on time.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Прибавить обороты, начать работать активнее» — move into a higher gear. Move into a higher stage — не устойчивое сочетание; про этапы говорят the next stage, но не a higher stage.

reply.context: A colleague says: "We're behind schedule and the client meeting is tomorrow morning."
options: I know — we all need to move up a gear this afternoon.
I know — we all need to move up a gear, so let's take a long lunch break.
Indeed; a marked elevation in operational tempo is now required of all personnel.
reply.explanationRu: Move up a gear значит «начать работать активнее», это противоречит предложению долгого перерыва во втором варианте. Третий звучит как приказ по учреждению, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The whole team needs to work much faster if we want to finish on time.
rewrite.frame: The whole team needs to ____ if we want to finish on time.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Начать работать быстрее и активнее» — move up a gear (или move into a higher gear).

definitionEn: something or someone considered especially good, valuable or delightful, often not widely known
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «настоящая находка, что-то особенно ценное» (a hidden gem); буквальное значение «драгоценный камень» проще и не тренируется.
situation: You want to say that a place, book, film or person is excellent and especially pleasing, sometimes without being famous.

examples.text: Tucked away behind the station, this little café is a real [[gem]].
Critics largely ignored the novel when it came out, but readers now consider it a hidden [[gem]].
Our new neighbour is an absolute [[gem]]; she waters our plants whenever we're away.

texts: This little bookshop is a real [[gem]] that tourists rarely find.
Their grandmother is an absolute [[gem]], always ready to help.
Beneath the boring cover lies a real narrative [[gem]] of a novel.

badCollocation.noteRu: Выгодную цену называют a bargain или a great deal, а не a gem. Gem — про качество и очарование места, вещи или человека, а не про низкую цену.

collocationTask.prompt: This tiny restaurant is a real ___ that most tourists never discover.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Прекрасное, но малоизвестное место — a real gem. Failure и flop — «провал», nuisance — «источник раздражения»; ни одно так не хвалят.

nuance.text: This tiny secondhand bookshop is a real [[gem]] that most visitors walk straight past.
nuance.explanationRu: Gem часто описывает небольшое, скромное, но обаятельное место или человека, особенно малоизвестные. Treasure звучит масштабнее и торжественнее — обычно про что-то само по себе ценное, а не малозаметное.

reverse.text: The museum's most famous [[treasure]] is a gold crown over a thousand years old.
reverse.explanationRu: Про по-настоящему ценный, знаменитый экспонат — treasure. Gem больше подходит для скромного, малоизвестного открытия, а не для главной драгоценности музея.

fixIt.text: Tucked away behind the station, this little café serves the best coffee in town — a real [[disaster]] that more people should discover.
fixIt.explanationRu: Лучший кофе в городе, который стоит открыть для себя, — это никак не disaster («катастрофа»). Такое место — a real gem.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Any recommendations for quiet places to eat near the old town?"
options: Yes! There's a tiny place on Elm Street — an absolute gem, hardly anyone knows it.
Yes! There's a tiny place on Elm Street — an absolute gem, the food gave me food poisoning.
Affirmative. One establishment on Elm Street constitutes a veritable culinary gem of considerable merit.
reply.explanationRu: Absolute gem — искренняя похвала месту, это противоречит отравлению едой во втором варианте. Третий звучит как отрывок из официального отчёта, а не совет другу.

rewrite.original: Nobody has heard of this little restaurant, but the food there is absolutely wonderful.
rewrite.frame: This little restaurant is a real ____ that nobody has heard of.

definitionEn: typical of a general type, rather than being special, original or sold under a brand name
situation: Something is typical of its whole category and lacks any special, original or distinctive features.

examples.text: The pharmacy recommended a [[generic]] version of the medicine, which costs far less than the branded one.
The film's plot felt so [[generic]] that I could predict every twist ten minutes in advance.
Instead of addressing my actual complaint, the company sent back a [[generic]] reply that could have been written for anyone.

texts: Why pay more for the branded version when the [[generic]] one works just as well?
Her design looked pleasant but oddly [[generic]], like a hundred others online.
We got a [[generic]] apology instead of a real explanation.

badCollocation.noteRu: Про людей generic почти не говорят: так называют товары, ответы, названия. Про скучного, ничем не примечательного человека скажут unremarkable или bland.

collocationTask.prompt: Rather than a real apology, customers received a ___ response copied to everyone.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Безликий, одинаковый для всех ответ — a generic response. Handwritten — «написанный от руки», confidential — «конфиденциальный», overdue — «просроченный»; ни одно не о шаблонности.

nuance.text: The advert felt utterly [[generic]], with none of the humour the brand is known for.
nuance.explanationRu: Generic — обезличенный, без индивидуальности, часто с оттенком критики. Standard — нейтральное «обычный, стандартный вариант», без критики за отсутствие оригинальности.

reverse.text: The hotel room was clean and had all the [[standard]] amenities you'd expect.
reverse.explanationRu: Нейтральный, ожидаемый набор удобств — standard. Generic здесь прозвучало бы как критика, а не нейтральное описание.

fixIt.text: The company sent back a [[personal]] reply that looked exactly like the one everyone else on the forum received, word for word.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Точно такой же, как у всех, слово в слово» противоречит personal (личный, индивидуальный). Безликий, одинаковый для всех ответ — generic.

wordFormation.text: Painkillers like this one are sold [[generically]] under dozens of different brand names.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "What did you think of the new company welcome email?"
options: Honestly, it felt pretty generic — like it was written for any company, not just ours.
Honestly, it felt pretty generic — so personal, like it was written just for me.
One might characterise the correspondence as regrettably devoid of bespoke particularity.
reply.explanationRu: Generic — обезличенный, шаблонный, это противоречит so personal во втором варианте. Третий звучит как канцелярский отзыв, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The reply didn't address my specific problem at all; it looked like a copy-paste template.
rewrite.frame: The reply was so ____ that it didn't address my specific problem at all.

definitionEn: to hit something at an angle and bounce off instead of going straight through or stopping
senseNote: Здесь — «скользнуть, отскочить, задев по касательной» (the ball glanced off the post); базовое значение «бросить быстрый взгляд» (glance at your watch) более распространено и не тренируется.
situation: A moving object hits something at an angle and bounces off instead of stopping or going straight through it.

examples.text: The shot [[glanced]] off the defender's boot and flew into the top corner.
The bullet [[glanced]] off the metal railing and shattered a nearby window instead of hitting its target.
The ball [[glanced]] off the crossbar and rolled agonisingly wide of the goal.

texts: The arrow [[glanced]] off the tree trunk and landed in the grass.
His fist [[glanced]] off my shoulder instead of landing properly.
The stone [[glanced]] off the water's surface three times before sinking.

badCollocation.text: the ball [[glanced]] straight through the net
badCollocation.noteRu: Glance off значит «скользнуть вбок, задев», а не пройти насквозь. Про мяч, влетевший точно в сеть, говорят go straight into или hit the net.

collocationTask.prompt: The bullet ___ off the car door and hit a nearby wall instead.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Задеть что-то и отскочить вбок — glance off. Exploded, surrendered и apologised по смыслу сюда вовсе не подходят.

nuance.text: The shot [[glanced]] off the post and rolled agonisingly along the goal line.
nuance.explanationRu: Glance off — задеть что-то по касательной, вскользь, и отклониться в сторону. Bounce — более общее «отскочить», необязательно вскользь и под углом; часто про полный отскок назад.

reverse.text: The ball [[bounced]] hard off the wall and came straight back to her.
reverse.explanationRu: Полный, прямой отскок назад — bounced. Glance off описывает скользящее касание под углом, а не прямой отскок обратно.

fixIt.text: The bullet [[pierced]] the metal railing at a sharp angle and flew off harmlessly in a completely different direction.
fixIt.explanationRu: Pierce значит «пробить насквозь», а тут «отлетела в другую сторону» — явное противоречие. Задеть и отклониться вбок — glanced off.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why didn't the goalkeeper save that shot? It looked easy."
options: It actually glanced off a defender at the last second, so he had no chance.
It actually glanced off a defender and stopped dead right there on the line.
The trajectory was in fact deflected by an intervening defensive player, rendering interception improbable.
reply.explanationRu: Glance off значит «задеть и отклониться», а не «остановиться на месте» (второй вариант). Третий звучит как технический комментарий, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: The stone hit the water at an angle and skipped across the surface twice.
rewrite.frame: The stone ____ off the water's surface twice before sinking.

definitionEn: a short experience that gives you a little understanding of something usually hidden from view
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «краткое, частичное понимание, проблеск» (a glimpse into someone's life/world); буквальное значение «мельком увиденное» (catch a glimpse of a bird) более базовое и не тренируется напрямую.
situation: Something briefly shows or explains a part of a person's life, feelings or a hidden world that you don't normally see.

examples.text: The documentary offers a rare [[glimpse]] into the daily lives of lighthouse keepers.
In the interview, the actress gave fans a brief [[glimpse]] into her struggles with anxiety.
Old family letters offer a fascinating [[glimpse]] into what daily life was like a century ago.

texts: The trailer gives us just a [[glimpse]] of what's to come.
Her diary offers a private [[glimpse]] into a difficult childhood.
The leaked photos gave the public an unexpected [[glimpse]] into the singer's home life.

badCollocation.text: a full [[glimpse]] of the whole process
badCollocation.noteRu: Glimpse по определению краткий, частичный взгляд; full glimpse звучит как противоречие. Полную картину называют a full picture или a complete view.

collocationTask.prompt: The new documentary offers a rare ___ into the president's daily routine.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Краткое, частичное представление о чём-то скрытом — a glimpse into something. Criticism, warning и apology по смыслу сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: The photo gave us a rare [[glimpse]] of the singer's life away from the cameras.
nuance.explanationRu: Glimpse — краткое, часто визуальное впечатление, не глубокое понимание. Insight — более глубокое понимание сути, необязательно краткое или визуальное; для одной случайной фотографии точнее glimpse.

reverse.text: Years studying the company gave her real [[insight]] into how such scandals happen.
reverse.explanationRu: Глубокое понимание, накопленное за годы, — insight. Glimpse описывает что-то краткое и частичное, а не результат долгого изучения.

fixIt.text: A single blurry photograph gave researchers rare [[insight]] into the extinct bird's exact colouring.
fixIt.explanationRu: Insight — глубокое понимание сути, а не то, что даёт одна размытая фотография. Краткое, частичное впечатление от одного снимка — a glimpse.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I watched that new documentary about the fashion industry last night."
options: Oh yes, it gives you a real glimpse into how exhausting that work actually is.
Oh yes, it gives you a real glimpse, they explain literally every single detail for six hours straight.
Indeed, the programme affords the viewer a most illuminating glimpse into said industry's inner workings.
reply.explanationRu: Glimpse — краткое, частичное впечатление, это противоречит «объясняют буквально всё за шесть часов» во втором варианте. Третий звучит как официальная рецензия, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The old photographs briefly show us what the city looked like before the war.
rewrite.frame: The old photographs give us a ____ of what the city looked like before the war.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Краткое представление о чём-то» — a glimpse of something.

definitionEn: used to emphasize how complete or spectacular something is, especially a failure or mistake
senseNote: Здесь — ироничное усиление: «феерический, оглушительный», обычно о провале или катастрофе (a glorious failure/mess); базовое значение «великолепный, прекрасный» (glorious weather) проще и не тренируется.
situation: Something went wrong in a spectacular, complete way, and you describe it with humorous exaggeration rather than simple disappointment.

examples.text: The product launch was a [[glorious]] disaster: the website crashed within minutes and half the stock was mislabelled.
My attempt at baking a wedding cake was a [[glorious]] failure that ended with icing on the ceiling.
Their plan to surprise her with a flash mob turned into a [[glorious]] mess when the music wouldn't start.

texts: The team's first attempt at cooking was a [[glorious]] failure.
His speech turned into a [[glorious]] car crash of forgotten lines.
Their road trip was a [[glorious]] disaster from start to finish.

badCollocation.noteRu: Glorious в этом ироничном значении подчёркивает масштаб: a glorious disaster/failure/mess. Со словом minor (незначительный) оно противоречит по смыслу.

collocationTask.prompt: The charity bake sale turned into a ___ disaster when the oven caught fire.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Glorious disaster — ироничное усиление масштаба провала. Minor, subtle и modest, наоборот, преуменьшают, поэтому сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: Our first attempt at making sushi was a [[glorious]] failure, but we laughed about it for weeks.
nuance.explanationRu: Glorious добавляет иронию и юмор к провалу, будто им можно почти гордиться. Total просто усиливает масштаб («полный провал») без этого шутливого оттенка.

reverse.text: The investigation revealed [[total]] failure at every level of management.
reverse.explanationRu: Серьёзный, невесёлый контекст расследования не подходит для шутливого glorious. Total здесь звучит уместно нейтрально и серьёзно.

fixIt.text: Our first attempt at making sushi was a [[minor]] failure that we still laugh about years later, because absolutely everything that could go wrong did.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Абсолютно всё пошло не так» противоречит minor (незначительный). Про провал такого масштаба, да ещё со смехом, — a glorious failure.

reply.context: A friend says: "How did the surprise party planning go?"
options: Honestly? A glorious disaster — the cake collapsed and the lights went out.
Honestly? A glorious disaster — everything went perfectly according to plan.
One might characterise the proceedings as a gloriously catastrophic undertaking, regrettably.
reply.explanationRu: Glorious disaster — ироничное «феерический провал», это противоречит «всё прошло идеально» во втором варианте. Третий звучит слишком книжно для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: The picnic was a complete disaster from start to finish, but it was actually pretty funny.
rewrite.frame: The picnic was a ____ disaster from start to finish, but it was actually pretty funny.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Феерический провал» с оттенком юмора — a glorious disaster.
